title: Check yourself: failing fast and failing safe

questions.stem: A Booking record's compact constructor holds `assert nights > 0 : "nights";`. Its unit test builds a booking of 0 nights, expects an AssertionError, and passes in the Maven build. In production the service runs as `java -jar booking.jar`. What happens to a booking of 0 nights there?

options.text: It is created, since javac leaves assert statements out of classes it compiles for packaging into a jar
options.says: the assert is compiled into the class: the same class throws when the JVM runs with -ea

options.text: It is refused with an AssertionError, since the JVM runs assert statements unless it was started with the -da flag
options.says: assertions are off by default: a plain java run creates the object, and only a JVM started with -ea runs the assert

options.text: It is created, since the JVM skips every assert statement unless it was started with the -ea flag
options.says: assertions are disabled unless the JVM runs with -ea; Surefire enables them for tests, so the test passes and production skips the check

options.text: It is refused with an AssertionError, since Surefire records the -ea flag in the manifest of the jar it builds
options.says: Surefire enables assertions for the tests it runs; a production JVM started without -ea skips the assert

origin.section: An Assertion Checks Nothing Unless the JVM Runs with -ea

questions.stem: An Invoice class stores its currency from the constructor without looking at it, and its formatTotal() starts with `Objects.requireNonNull(currency, "currency")`. At 09:00 a billing import creates an invoice with no currency. At 23:00 a PDF job calls formatTotal() on it, and the exception is logged. Whose calls does the logged stack trace show?

options.text: The PDF job's calls from 23:00, since Java 21 trims a trace down to the frames of the most recent job
options.says: the import's frames are absent because the constructor had already returned when the exception was created

options.text: The PDF job's calls from 23:00, since the import's calls left the stack when the Invoice constructor returned
options.says: a trace holds the frames on the stack when the exception is created; only the PDF job's calls lead to formatTotal() at 23:00

options.text: The billing import's calls from 09:00, since requireNonNull reports where the currency field was set to null
options.says: requireNonNull throws where it is called, in formatTotal() at 23:00; its message is only the text it was given

options.text: The billing import's calls from 09:00, since an Invoice keeps the stack of the code that created it
options.says: an object keeps no record of its creator's stack; the trace is taken when the exception is created

origin.section: A Null Stored Now Fails Later, in a Trace That Doesn't Name Who Stored It

questions.stem: A service reads `int ttl = Integer.parseInt(file.getProperty("cache.ttl.s", "300"));` and then calls `log.warn("unknown setting " + k)` for each key k in the file that it has no use for. During an incident an operator adds `cache.ttl.sec=5` to the file and restarts the service. What TTL does the service run with?

options.text: A 5 s TTL, since the file's only TTL line now holds 5 and getProperty returns that line's value
options.says: getProperty returns the value stored under the exact key it is given; the line is stored under cache.ttl.sec, not cache.ttl.s

options.text: A 300 s TTL, since log.warn on cache.ttl.sec resets cache.ttl.s to the value written in the code
options.says: the warning only writes a line; 300 comes from the lookup of cache.ttl.s finding no such key

options.text: A 5 s TTL, since getProperty for cache.ttl.s matches cache.ttl.sec as the closest key in the file
options.says: getProperty looks up the exact key it is given; cache.ttl.s is absent, so it returns the default

options.text: A 300 s TTL, since getProperty for cache.ttl.s finds no such key in the file and falls back
options.says: the misspelt key is never asked for, so getProperty returns the default and the service runs with 300 s after a warning

origin.section: A Default Also Hides a Misspelt Key, Unless Unknown Keys Stop the Start

questions.stem: A worker sizes its pool with `int size; try { size = Integer.parseInt(props.getProperty("pool.size", "8")); } catch (NumberFormatException e) { size = 8; }`. An operator sets `pool.size=32 threads` in the file and restarts the worker. How many threads does the pool get?

options.text: 32, since parseInt reads the leading digits and the catch block is reached only when there are none
options.says: parseInt refuses the whole string, as "800ms" shows on the page; it does not stop at a letter

options.text: 8, since getProperty hands back its default for a value that is not made of digits alone
options.says: getProperty returns the stored string as it is; the page's "800ms" reached parseInt unchanged

options.text: 32, since Properties.load keeps only the first word of a value, so the catch block never runs
options.says: Properties.load stores the whole value "32 threads", and parseInt refuses it

options.text: 8, since parseInt throws on the whole value and the catch block hands back the default
options.says: parseInt throws NumberFormatException on the whole value, and the catch turns the failure into the silent default

origin.section: A Default Also Hides a Misspelt Key, Unless Unknown Keys Stop the Start
